# Accessibility Design Review: `DataLoader` **VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The `DataLoader` component handles state transitions purely visually and fails to communicate dynamic loading and loaded states to assistive technology. Without a persistent live region, `aria-busy`, or status announcements, screen reader users are left unaware when content updates have completed. Additionally, the CSS spinner features an indefinite looping animation with no accommodation for users with vestibular motion sensitivities. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions Based on typical dynamic loading components: - **Predicted**: Missing `aria-live` announcement region or `role="status"`. *(Confirmed)* - **Predicted**: Missing `aria-busy` attribute on the dynamic container during fetch. *(Confirmed)* - **Predicted**: Silent content insertion upon data resolution (WCAG 4.1.3 failure). *(Confirmed)* - **Predicted**: Infinite CSS spinner animation lacking `prefers-reduced-motion` safeguards. *(Confirmed)* - **Predicted**: Missing error state handling for failed requests. *(Confirmed)* --- ### Findings #### Major Findings (Significantly degrades experience) 1. **Dynamic content updates and loading completion are silent to assistive technology** - **Evidence**: `DataLoader.jsx:15-28` ```jsx
{isLoading && (
...
)} {!isLoading && data && (
...
)}
``` - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS). - **Standard/Criteria**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA), WCAG SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A), WAI-ARIA Dynamic Content & Live Regions. - **Why this matters**: When the component mounts, a screen reader may read "Loading data..." if focused or virtual-cursor navigated, but once the asynchronous operation finishes 2 seconds later, the DOM replacement occurs silently. A blind user has no way of knowing whether the request is still pending, completed, or failed unless they re-browse the DOM. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Provide a persistent live container with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-busy={isLoading}` rather than mounting/unmounting ad-hoc wrappers. When `isLoading` transitions to `false`, the live container notifies the assistive technology of new content. ```jsx
{isLoading ? (

Loading data...

) : ( data && (

Results

{data.content}

) )}
``` ```yaml ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: dynamic-loading-silent-status fingerprint: a11e89b4f2c031d7 source: DataLoader.jsx:15 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA) section_508_fpc_context: not in scope severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, cognitive=MEDIUM evidence: DataLoader.jsx lines 15-28 render conditional blocks inside an unadorned div with no role="status", aria-live, or aria-busy. reproduction_steps: 1. Mount DataLoader with a screen reader running (VoiceOver/NVDA). 2. Wait 2000ms for data resolution. 3. Observe screen reader speech log. expected_behavior: Status transition or newly loaded results should be politely announced to assistive technology. actual_behavior: The DOM updates silently; no speech synthesizer output is triggered. trend: new ``` --- #### Minor Findings (Friction but workaround exists) 1. **Spinner infinite rotation does not honor `prefers-reduced-motion`** - **Evidence**: `DataLoader.css:25-33` ```css .spinner { ... animation: spin 1s linear infinite; } ``` - **User Group Impacted**: Users with vestibular disorders or motion triggers. - **Standard/Criteria**: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A), WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (Level AAA context). - **Why this matters**: In network failure cases, slow connections, or extended loading, continuous spinning without an opt-out can cause nausea, dizziness, or distraction for motion-sensitive users. - **Fix**: Wrap the animation in a media query or suppress rotation when reduced motion is preferred: ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .spinner { animation: none; border-top-color: #0066cc; /* Render a static indicator */ } } ``` 2. **Visual spinner element is not hidden from the accessibility tree** - **Evidence**: `DataLoader.jsx:17` ```jsx
``` - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users. - **Standard/Criteria**: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A). - **Why this matters**: While an empty `div` usually generates no accessible node, some screen readers or browser combinations expose empty styled elements as generic artifacts. Explicit decorative hygiene prevents synthetic anomalies. - **Fix**: Explicitly set `aria-hidden="true"` on the visual CSS icon: `
`. --- #### Enhancements (Best practice not met) 1. **Missing error state & timeout resilience**: The current implementation assumes the async operation always succeeds. If an error occurs, there is neither visual indication nor an `aria-live="assertive"` / `role="alert"` announcement to inform cognitive and screen reader users that fetching stopped. --- ### What's Missing - **Persistent Live Region Container**: Live regions must pre-exist in the DOM structure before content updates happen; dynamically injecting an element with `role="status"` or `aria-live` at the moment of completion is frequently ignored by VoiceOver and NVDA. - **`aria-busy` state tracking**: Assistive technologies can refrain from announcing partial updates until `aria-busy="false"`. - **Loading Failure Communication**: Lack of error recovery, timeout alerts, or retry affordances. --- ### Multi-Perspective Review | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | **HIGH** | Content switches asynchronously without live region or status announcement | | Keyboard-only | **LOW** | No interactive controls or focusable elements involved in this fixture | | Low vision | **LOW** | Layout is clean; `#0066cc` provides 4.5:1 contrast against white background | | Cognitive | **MEDIUM** | Indefinite wait state if request hangs; no clear timeout or failure indicator | | Vestibular & motion | **MEDIUM** | Continuous infinite spinning animation without `prefers-reduced-motion` | | Auditory access | **LOW** | No audio or video content | | Environmental contrast | **LOW** | Text and borders meet standard minimums | - **Screen reader user**: User hears "Loading data..." initially, but never receives notification that "Results: Loaded data" has finished rendering. - **Keyboard-only user**: No interactive traps or navigation barriers, as the component currently consists of passive text. - **Low vision user**: Visible text has sufficient contrast; spinner is legible. - **Vestibular sensitivity**: Spinner spins continuously until data resolves. If the request stalls, the spinner loops indefinitely. --- ### Verdict Justification **Verdict: REVISE** - **Reason**: The component violates WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and SC 4.1.2. The lack of `aria-busy` and absence of an established `aria-live` polite region means screen reader users miss the core purpose of the component—knowing when data loading has succeeded. - **Path to ACCEPT**: 1. Wrap the container in `aria-live="polite"` and tie `aria-busy={isLoading}`. 2. Mark the spinning element `aria-hidden="true"`. 3. Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to disable the CSS rotation animation. 4. Include basic error state feedback if the async request fails. --- ### Open Questions (Unscored) 1. *Context of trigger*: Is this `DataLoader` triggered by a user action (such as a search button or tab switch), or does it run on initial page load? If triggered by a button, focus management may also be required once content loads.
